Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Create a concise, denominator-first evidence card in the “Connector-access-check archive” for future Helio Start operating reviews. Summarize what the first fully mature post-check cohort established about credential-related failures, and clearly separate that operational finding from any longer-horizon business outcomes the cohort did not establish.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "create_doc", "arguments": {"title": "Helio Start connector-access check — first mature cohort evidence card", "body": "# Helio Start connector-access check — first mature cohort

**Denominators first.** Of 92 completed applications, 68 were admitted, 15 were pending or assisted for missing/uncertain connector authority, and 9 had other assisted or ineligible outcomes. Among the 68 admitted workspaces with mature day-7 windows, 59 completed a supported first integration (86.8%); 9 did not. Three of those 9 nonactivators (33.3%) had credential-related stalls. In the prior comparison group, 18 of 147 admitted workspaces (12.2%) had credential-related stalls. The post-check cohort also generated 11 support contacts across 8 admitted workspaces.

**Operational finding.** Credential-related stalls were present among post-check nonactivators, but were not the only reason for nonactivation. The 15 cases routed for missing or uncertain authority are a separate pre-admission group, not admitted-workspace failures. These descriptive counts establish what was observed in this cohort; they do not establish that the check caused a change versus the prior group.

**Not established.** This day-7 operating evidence does not establish first-paid conversion, day-90 retention, revenue, paid-acquisition performance, or other longer-horizon business outcomes. Keep those claims separate until their own mature evidence is available.", "folder": "Connector-access-check archive"}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_170_02", "path": "args", "criterion": "The body gives a denominator-first comparison for credential-related failures among admitted workspaces: 3 of 68 in the first fully mature cohort after the connector-access check (about 4.4%) versus 18 of 147 in the prior cohort (about 12.2%). It accurately interprets the lower post-check rate as operational evidence supporting the connector-access check, without presenting the comparison as proof of broader causality.

The body clearly and explicitly states that the mature-cohort result did not establish mature retention, paid conversion, or revenue performance. Missing any of these three limitations, or claiming that any was established, must fail.", "value": {"title": "Helio Start connector-access check — first mature cohort evidence card", "body": "# Helio Start connector-access check — first mature cohort

**Denominators first.** Of 92 completed applications, 68 were admitted, 15 were pending or assisted for missing/uncertain connector authority, and 9 had other assisted or ineligible outcomes. Among the 68 admitted workspaces with mature day-7 windows, 59 completed a supported first integration (86.8%); 9 did not. Three of those 9 nonactivators (33.3%) had credential-related stalls. In the prior comparison group, 18 of 147 admitted workspaces (12.2%) had credential-related stalls. The post-check cohort also generated 11 support contacts across 8 admitted workspaces.

**Operational finding.** Credential-related stalls were present among post-check nonactivators, but were not the only reason for nonactivation. The 15 cases routed for missing or uncertain authority are a separate pre-admission group, not admitted-workspace failures. These descriptive counts establish what was observed in this cohort; they do not establish that the check caused a change versus the prior group.

However, it does not explicitly interpret the post-check admitted-workspace rate of 3/68 (about 4.4%) as lower than 18/147 (12.2%) or as operational evidence supporting the connector-access check; it only describes the observations and disclaims causality."}]}
